# Quality rules

These are the rules `npx @ballmac/cli check` and the MCP tool `audit_project` apply to your own source. Build to them from the first draft, then run the check when you finish.

## states/ballmac-state-prop (warn)

**A Ballmac component with states is used without a state prop.** The component can show a loading skeleton, an empty message and an error with a retry, but this use only ever shows the ready view. When the request is slow or fails, people see a blank area or a frozen screen.

Fix: Pass `state` from your data hook, for example state={isPending ? "loading" : isError ? "error" : rows.length ? "ready" : "empty"} and onRetry={refetch}.

```tsx
// Bad
<DashboardPro1 />

// Good
<DashboardPro1 state={isPending ? "loading" : isError ? "error" : "ready"} onRetry={refetch} />
```

## states/data-without-states (warn)

**A component fetches data but never reads loading or error state.** While the request is running, or if it fails, the screen has nothing to show. That is the first thing a person sees on a slow connection.

Fix: Read the loading and error values the hook returns (isPending, isError, error), render a skeleton for loading and a message with a retry for errors, and an empty state when there is no data.

```tsx
// Bad
const { data } = useQuery(...)
return <List items={data} />

// Good
const { data, isPending, isError, refetch } = useQuery(...)
if (isPending) return <ListSkeleton />
if (isError) return <ErrorState onRetry={refetch} />
return <List items={data} />
```

## a11y/img-alt (error)

**An image has no alt attribute.** Screen reader users hear the file name or nothing. Search engines and failed loads show nothing useful either.

Fix: Add alt with a short description of what the image shows, or alt="" if it is purely decorative.

```tsx
// Bad
<img src="/hero.png" />

// Good
<img src="/hero.png" alt="The dashboard with a revenue chart" />
```

## a11y/control-name (error)

**A button or link has an icon but no accessible name.** Screen reader users hear only “button” with no hint of what it does, and voice control users cannot say its name.

Fix: Add aria-label="What it does" to the control, or include visually hidden text such as <span className="sr-only">Close</span>.

```tsx
// Bad
<button onClick={close}><XIcon /></button>

// Good
<button onClick={close} aria-label="Close"><XIcon aria-hidden="true" /></button>
```

## a11y/clickable-non-interactive (error)

**A click handler is on an element that keyboards cannot reach.** A <div> with onClick cannot be focused or activated with the keyboard, and screen readers do not announce it as something to press.

Fix: Use a <button> (or <a> for navigation). If it truly must stay a div, add role, tabIndex={0} and onKeyDown for Enter and Space.

```tsx
// Bad
<div onClick={open}>Open</div>

// Good
<button type="button" onClick={open}>Open</button>
```

## a11y/focus-outline-removed (error)

**The focus outline is removed and nothing replaces it.** Keyboard users lose track of where they are. It is one of the most common ways an app becomes unusable without a mouse.

Fix: Keep the default outline, or replace it with a visible style such as focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring.

```tsx
// Bad
<button className="outline-none">

// Good
<button className="outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring">
```

## a11y/input-label (warn)

**A form field has no label.** A placeholder disappears as soon as someone types and is not a label. Screen readers announce an unnamed field, and clicking the text does not focus it.

Fix: Add <label htmlFor="id"> that matches the field's id, wrap the field in a <label>, or add aria-label.

```tsx
// Bad
<input placeholder="Email" />

// Good
<label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" />
```

## a11y/positive-tabindex (error)

**tabIndex is greater than zero.** It pulls the element to the front of the tab order, so focus jumps around the page in a way nobody expects.

Fix: Use tabIndex={0} to make an element focusable in its natural place, or tabIndex={-1} to focus it from code only.

## a11y/hand-rolled-dialog (warn)

**A full-screen overlay is built by hand.** A hand-made modal usually misses the focus trap, Escape to close, scroll lock and the dialog role, so keyboard and screen reader users get stuck behind it.

Fix: Use the Dialog, Sheet or Drawer component (Radix-based), which does all of that.

```tsx
// Bad
<div className="fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/50">…</div>

// Good
<Dialog><DialogContent>…</DialogContent></Dialog>
```

## a11y/link-no-href (warn)

**A link has no href.** An <a> without href is not focusable or announced as a link. People cannot open it in a new tab or copy its address.

Fix: Add an href, or use a <button> if it performs an action instead of navigating.

## tokens/hardcoded-color (warn)

**A fixed colour is used instead of a theme token.** Fixed colours do not follow the theme, so dark mode and any re-theming break: white panels glowing in the dark, grey text that cannot be read.

Fix: Use token classes: bg-background, bg-card, text-foreground, text-muted-foreground, border-border, bg-primary, text-destructive.

```tsx
// Bad
className="bg-white text-gray-900 border-gray-200"

// Good
className="bg-background text-foreground border-border"
```

## motion/endless-decorative (warn)

**A decorative animation runs forever and ignores reduced motion.** People with vestibular disorders turn on “reduce motion” because endless movement makes them ill. An animation that ignores the setting is an accessibility bug.

Fix: Add motion-reduce:animate-none to the class, wrap the Motion loop in useReducedMotion, or put the CSS animation inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

```tsx
// Bad
<span className="animate-ping" />

// Good
<span className="animate-ping motion-reduce:animate-none" />
```

## layout/fixed-wide (warn)

**A fixed width is wider than a small phone.** A phone is 360 to 390 pixels wide. A fixed 480px element makes the whole page scroll sideways.

Fix: Add max-w-full, or make the width responsive: w-full md:w-[480px].

```tsx
// Bad
<div className="w-[480px]">

// Good
<div className="w-full max-w-[480px]">
```

## layout/viewport-height (info)

**h-screen is used for a full-height layout.** On phones, 100vh includes the area behind the browser's address bar, so the bottom of the page is cut off.

Fix: Use min-h-dvh or h-dvh, which follow the visible area.

## rtl/physical-direction (off)

**A left or right class will not mirror in right-to-left languages.** In Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu the layout should be mirrored. Fixed left and right spacing leaves margins and icons on the wrong side.

Fix: Use logical classes: ms-/me- instead of ml-/mr-, ps-/pe- instead of pl-/pr-, text-start/text-end, start-/end- instead of left-/right-.
